acme_prod: Hey—our prod project (org=org-8112, project=search-api) showed 0 monthly credits at midnight UTC but traffic kept succeeding until ~02:10 and then we started getting 429s. Around 03:15 a partial refill appeared (not full). We use long-running websocket streams for generation. Could streaming be consuming next-cycle credits early? cc @emma_support :thinking:

emma_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the org/project and any x- headers from a successful request? Also did you see any `x-credits-remaining` / `x-reset-time` headers on responses? :eyes:

acme_prod: org-8112, project=search-api. Example response headers from a successful request at 00:45 UTC: `x-credits-remaining: 0`, `x-reset-time: 1715001600` (which we expected to be 00:00 UTC). Then at 02:12 we got `429` and no x-headers. At 03:15 a later call returned `x-credits-remaining: 1200`. We didn't change anything.

dmitri_infra: Quick summary from infra side: we track separate counters for generation tokens vs embedding tokens and a short-lived allocation window for streaming sessions (to avoid stalls). Typically streaming sessions reserve a small token budget at request start, then consume as tokens are produced. Two things that can cause this behavior: (1) UI/tenant display caching (frontend cache TTL ~15m) and (2) our streaming allocation bug where an in-flight stream that crosses reset boundaries can be reconciled into the wrong cycle in rare timing cases (esp around DST/offset adjustments).

acme_prod: Ah ok. How do we repro or confirm this on our side? We want to show logs to our security team.

emma_support: Steps we usually ask customers to run to reproduce quickly: 1) start a long websocket/generate session ~10–30m before your expected reset; 2) keep it open across reset; 3) call a simple status endpoint after reset and capture response headers. Example curl for status (non-streaming):

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Org-ID: org-8112" \
  -H "X-Project: search-api" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/status
```

Look for `x-credits-remaining` and `x-reset-time`. If the long stream holds a reservation, you may see the stream succeed while the status shows 0. If you can reproduce, attach a packet/log trace.

acme_prod: Trying now, I'll run a 90m stream tonight spanning our reset and post headers.

billing-bot: automated: org org-8112 monthly credits refilled at 1715001600 (2024-05-06T00:00:00Z).

emma_support: Thanks — if you can reproduce, please include the websocket connection start/stop timestamps and the response headers. Meanwhile I'll open an infra ticket and tag @dmitri_infra to look for cross-cycle reconciliation issues.

dmitri_infra: Filed INF-5921: streaming allocation reconciliation occasionally attributed to pre-reset cycle when connection close/keepalive timing overlaps reset. Workaround for now: if you can, prefer short-lived streams or set polling frequency to re-check headers after reset. We're also going to add a diagnostic header `x-stream-reservation: <ms>` next deploy to show reservation window.

acme_prod: Got it — we'll try repro tonight. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

emma_support: Also note an interim workaround: enable reserved capacity (Dedicated) if you need strict deterministic behavior across resets — that avoids the shared streaming reservation logic. Happy to coordinate an escalation if you hit it again.

acme_prod: Thanks — will report back with logs.

emma_support: marking follow-up: collect headers + websocket start/stop + any `429` traces. I'll keep you posted.
